name: config_resource_delete

name.note: required for a named resourceType, empty for a singleton

collection.note: the core collection: an omitted or empty value means core, and the Tool sends collection=core on every Gateway read and write it makes; any other value fails with invalid_argument before anything is dispatched (D30 owner ruling 5)

preconditionToken.nativeLocation: the DELETE path itself: the signature is the route's last path parameter

targetId.collection: the core collection only: the reads and the documented DELETE route name it as the collection query parameter (the route's path carries the Target and the signature, and it takes no request body), so a Target is <resourceType>/<name> in that collection; a caller-supplied collection is accepted only when it is core, and any other value fails with invalid_argument before anything is dispatched (D30 owner ruling 5)
targetId.denialCodeSource: D30 §7, Tool-scoped; the Phase 3 machinery keeps operation_disabled

reservedResourceNames.match: the whole name, trimmed and compared case-insensitively, never a substring: `IgnitionMCPPolicyStaging` is a different resource and stays manageable. Fail-closed on case because Ignition documents no rule for how two config resource names compare, and the refusal names the *reserved* spelling however the caller wrote it.
reservedResourceNames.rule: D30 owner ruling 4: this resource is the Tag provider that holds the Runtime Target Policy, and a generic config Mutation refuses it **by name** before the Target allowlist is consulted — even under an explicit `*` — because `ignition/tag-provider` is an allowed type and nothing else would stop a delete or a reconfiguration of the policy's storage provider. It is a refusal by name *within* an allowed type, not an entry in the Refused resource types set (D30 §5): the type stays allowed and every other Tag provider stays manageable through this Tool. The refusal is Mutation-only, so `config_resource_get` still serves the resource.

fixedKnobsNote: The documented DELETE route takes an optional `confirm` flag for a delete the Gateway says would affect other resources. The caller cannot choose it: it is never sent, so such a delete is refused like any other rejection and no call can authorize a cascade outside its Targets. The route's `collection` query parameter is the other fixed knob: it is always `core` (D30 owner ruling 5).

requestSchemaValidation.schema: not applicable: the documented DELETE route takes no request body, and nothing but the path is sent
requestSchemaValidation.appliesTo: the Target identity and the Resource signature, validated and percent-encoded before dispatch
requestSchemaValidation.unavailableDisposition: a documented delete route whose Target cannot be read back exposes no delete route, so the Tool refuses the resource type with unsupported_capability

rejectionPolicy.rule: D30 §2: an explicit Gateway rejection is the result of the attempt — a 4xx (including 409 for a stale signature, which D30 §7 maps to `conflict`) or a 2xx carrying success=false with a problem. No read-back may turn it into a success: a Target that is gone may have been deleted by another writer.
verificationMaySucceedWhen: the Gateway claimed success (2xx with no refusal)
rejectionPolicy.ambiguousAttribution: a competing writer cannot be ruled out for an ambiguous dispatch, so a read-back that shows the Target gone is outcome_unknown, never a success; the Target still holding the caller's signature is not_applied

verification: bounded re-read of the Target: the claimed success is confirmed only when no resource exists at it, and the absence is reported as the Observed state
